problem_motivation.content: Prior calculations had not addressed the stability of 2D h-CuI on open graphene substrates.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Published calculations thus considered the freestanding monolayer [17,23] and the encapsulated layer [26,28] but not yet 2D h-CuI on an open graphene substrate

prior_approach.content: Mustonen et al. reported comparable anisotropy for graphene-encapsulated 2D h-CuI.
prior_approach.evidence_span: whereas Mustonen et al. [26] report a comparable anisotropy for graphene-encapsulated 2D h-CuI.

prior_approach.content: Prior wet-chemical route did not produce h-CuI on open monolayer regions.
prior_approach.evidence_span: the absence of h-CuI on open monolayer regions in the wet-chemical route [26]

prior_approach.content: Earlier work studied freestanding and encapsulated h-CuI via simulations/calculations.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Simulations find the freestanding lattice to be dynamically stable at room temperature [17,23]. A stabilizing effect of encapsulation in bilayer graphene was found in AIMD simulations... Published calculations thus considered the freestanding monolayer [17,23] and the encapsulated layer [26,28]

prior_approach.content: The deposition uses the previously reported Double Self-Assembly method.
Main-text adhesion values were obtained by direct DFT on an untwisted 3×3 h-CuI/5×5 graphene supercell.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The primary adhesion values used in the main text were obtained by direct DFT in the untwisted 3 × 3 h-CuI on 5 × 5 graphene supercell

prior_approach.content: Ullah et al. computed registry-dependent stacking energy of CuI encapsulated by graphene via sliding and rotating configurations.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Ullah et al. [S11], who computed the registry-dependent stacking energy of CuI encapsulated by graphene by sliding and rotating the layers across five distinct configurations

rejected_alternative.content: Routes based on CuI sublimation that produce γ-CuI are not operative here because temperatures stay far below appreciable CuI sublimation.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Furthermore, routes that yield γ-CuI nanosheets and epitaxial γ-CuI films sublime CuI powder from sources held at 360–450 °C [24,25]; in our process no component exceeds 180 °C, far below appreciable CuI sublimation, so the molecular CuI flux that enables γ-phase growth is absent.

rejected_alternative.content: An outer-surface adsorption model is ruled out because both domains would then be templated by the same outer sheet.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: A crystallite adsorbed on the outer surface would be templated by the outermost sheet, which is the same sheet for both domains. Registry with different sheets from within one plane is available only in the gallery

inspiration_source.content: The compression step was modeled on the Langmuir–Blodgett process.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: The compression was analogous to the Langmuir–Blodgett process

causal_claim.content: HI vapor reduces oxo-G to r-oxo-G and attacks the copper grid to supply copper.
causal_claim.evidence_span: where HI serves a dual purpose: it reduces the oxo-G to reduced oxo-graphene (r-oxo-G) [30], and it attacks the copper of the grid, the solid-state copper source of the synthesis.

causal_claim.content: Copper diffusion on graphene and meeting adsorbed iodine causes h-CuI nucleation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The copper released from the grid crosses the graphene by surface diffusion, on a potential energy landscape flat enough for copper adatoms to migrate anomalously at room temperature [32], and meets the iodine adsorbed during the HI treatment, where small hexagonal CuI (h-CuI) crystallites nucleate.

causal_claim.content: Annealing at 180 °C grows crystallites into extended vdW-epitaxial domains.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In the second step, annealing at 180 °C grows the crystallites into extended, van der Waals-epitaxial domains.

causal_claim.content: Thermal annealing improves crystallinity and promotes lattice relaxation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Thermal annealing at 180 °C significantly improves crystallinity and promotes lattice relaxation.

causal_claim.content: Small early-stage nuclei have little in-plane anisotropy because directional adaptation has not yet developed.
causal_claim.evidence_span: We attribute the near-absence of in-plane anisotropy to the early stage of growth: the nucleus is small and has a high edge-to-area ratio, so its lattice has not yet developed the directional adaptation that characterizes larger, fully grown domains.

causal_claim.content: Thermal annealing promotes further growth of intercalated domains.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Thermal annealing at 180 °C promotes the further growth of these intercalated domains

causal_claim.content: The anisotropy reflects uniaxial lattice adaptation to the epitaxial template, with perpendicular relaxation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The anisotropy of 1.7% indicates the uniaxial strain profile, reflecting the lattice adaptation to the epitaxial template in only one direction, while h-CuI remains relaxed in the perpendicular direction

causal_claim.content: If h-CuI were on the outer bilayer surface, registry with different graphene layers would be impossible; observed differing lock-in therefore implies encapsulation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: A crystallite on an outer surface of bilayer graphene would be templated by the outermost sheet in both cases, so registry with different graphene layers would be impossible. Both crystals are shown together in one image in Fig. S2, identifying the h-CuI as encapsulated within two graphene sheets

causal_claim.content: Thermal annealing reduces oxygen signal, indicating removal of oxygen groups and adsorbed water.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Thermal annealing significantly reduces the oxygen signal in the EDX maps (see Fig. S1e), indicating the effective removal of oxygen-containing functional groups and adsorbed water from the initial oxo-G template during the HI treatment and subsequent annealing.

causal_claim.content: The hexagonal phase forms because conditions for γ-CuI nucleation do not arise.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The conditions under which γ-CuI nucleates do not arise in the first place.

causal_claim.content: Interfacial adlayers strongly affect epitaxial growth by reducing adhesion when they increase interface spacing.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In contrast, interfacial adlayers have a pronounced effect on the epitaxial growth... An adlayer that increases the interfacial distance by Δz reduces the recovered adhesion to EvdW(z0 + Δz).

causal_claim.content: A single interfacial adlayer reduces recovered adhesion to only 10–17% of the original, insufficient to offset h-CuI metastability.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Inserting Δz = 2.8–3.7 Å into Eq. (2) leaves a recovered adhesion of only 1.4–2.3 meV/Å2, that is 10–17% of E0, which cannot compensate the 20.5 meV/Å2 by which the 2D phase lies above bulk γ-CuI.

causal_claim.content: Within bilayers, vdW pressure expels some adsorbates and presses layers together, supporting binding.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Within a bilayer, the van der Waals pressure expels part of the adsorbates into pockets [42,43] and presses the layers together, supporting the binding where adsorbates cannot be removed.

causal_claim.content: Where adsorbates remain, adhesion is not recovered and growth stops.
causal_claim.evidence_span: where adsorbates remain on the surface, the adhesion term of Eq. (1) is not recovered and growth stops.

causal_claim.content: Domain size correlates with local interface cleanliness and crystals extend until the next adsorbate.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The lateral domain size therefore correlates with the local cleanliness of the interface, as seen in Fig. S2, where the h-CuI crystals extend up to the next adsorbate on the surface.

causal_claim.content: On clean interfaces, further growth should mainly be limited by precursor supply.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Where the interface is clean, further growth is expected to be limited mainly by precursor supply to the graphene–CuI interface.

causal_claim.content: A single graphene layer damps relative out-of-plane h-CuI motion by about an order of magnitude.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Thus, a single graphene layer damps the relative out-of-plane movement of h-CuI between 1.20 and 1.55 THz by an order of magnitude in normalized power.

causal_claim.content: A second graphene interface stiffens the in-plane transverse optical mode of h-CuI.
causal_claim.evidence_span: For this collective in-plane movement, a second interface stiffens the h-CuI sheet.

causal_claim.content: Hexagonal order at 600 K is maintained mainly by the iodine framework while the copper sublattice can delocalize within it.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The hexagonal order is still maintained at 600 K, mainly by the iodine framework, while the copper sublattice may delocalize inside it.

causal_claim.content: Copper exhibits enhanced in-plane mobility within an iodine-maintained framework.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The copper therefore exhibits enhanced in-plane mobility within a framework maintained by the iodine sublattice.

causal_claim.content: Graphene's vdW spring damps out-of-plane motion of the nearby iodine sublayer.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The vdW spring of graphene thus damps the out-of-plane movement of the iodine sublayer in its vicinity.

causal_claim.content: In BLG both h-CuI sublayers are damped; in SLG damping is asymmetric and stronger at the graphene-contacting sublayer.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In BLG this damping is observed for both sublayers of h-CuI; in SLG the damping is asymmetric and stronger on the sublayer in direct contact with graphene.

causal_claim.content: HI vapor treatment both reduces oxo-G and starts nucleation of small h-CuI crystallites.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This treatment reduces the oxo-G and simultaneously initiates the nucleation of small h-CuI crystallites

causal_claim.content: Thermal annealing promotes reaction of iodine and copper, producing extended, well-defined h-CuI crystals.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the sample undergoes thermal annealing at 180 °C, which promotes the reaction between iodine and copper to form extended, well-defined h-CuI crystals

causal_claim.content: SDS compression causes flakes to assemble into a stable compact monolayer film.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This process caused the flakes to form a stable, compact, and uniform monolayer film.

causal_claim.content: The absence of h-CuI on gold confirms copper from the Cu TEM grid is the copper source.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The absence of h-CuI formation on the Au grid confirms that the copper from the Cu TEM grid is the sole source of Cu atoms in our synthesis

causal_claim.content: Contaminated surrounding regions limit domain growth and cause domain termination.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The domains terminate where they meet these contaminated regions, consistent with the contamination-limited growth identified in the Formation Mechanism and Stability section of the main text.

causal_claim.content: Alignment to different sheets within one plane implies the crystallites are in the bilayer gallery.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Registry with different sheets from within one plane is available only in the gallery, which places the bilayer crystallites between the graphene layers.

causal_claim.content: One graphene interface reduces the h-CuI versus bulk γ-CuI energy difference but leaves supported h-CuI metastable.
causal_claim.evidence_span: One graphene interface (13.58 meV/Å2) reduces the energy difference of h-CuI and bulk γ-CuI, however leaving the h-CuI/SLG heterostructure still about +7.0 meV/Å2 above γ (metastable, kinetically trapped)

causal_claim.content: A second graphene interface further lowers the energy difference, making h-CuI thermodynamically favored.
causal_claim.evidence_span: a second interface further reduces the energy difference to −6.6 meV/Å2 (thermodynamically favored)

causal_claim.content: Adhesion decays strongly with increased interface spacing because of the z^-4 tail.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The adhesion decays steeply due to the z−4 tail.

causal_claim.content: Such interfacial layers strongly reduce vdW stabilization needed for supported h-CuI growth.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Such an interfacial layer therefore strongly reduces the van der Waals stabilization required for growth of supported h-CuI.

mechanism_principle.content: A thin adsorbed interfacial film exists because HI vapor comes from aqueous solution and oxo-group reduction releases water.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since the vapor comes from an aqueous HI solution and the reduction of the oxo-groups releases water, a thin adsorbed film is present at the interface during this step

mechanism_principle.content: The preferred 30° offset comes from registry where iodine sits at graphene hexagon centers.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Physically, the 30° offset reflects the energetically preferred registry in which the iodine atoms occupy the centers of the graphene hexagons [26]

mechanism_principle.content: Formation depends on accessible routes, not only thermodynamics.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Its formation, however, is governed not only by thermodynamics but also by the available formation routes.

mechanism_principle.content: γ-CuI formation is unlikely because it would require a 3D nucleus with dangling bonds and sufficient supersaturation, which the process does not provide.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: First, the formation of γ-CuI would require a three-dimensional nucleus with dangling bonds... Thus, CuI forms in situ under dilute conditions, and the local supersaturation required to nucleate a three-dimensional γ-CuI particle is unlikely to be reached.

mechanism_principle.content: Multilayer growth is unlikely because h-CuI basal planes are self-saturating and precursors are supplied on graphene rather than atop h-CuI.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Second, the h-CuI surface is self-saturating: its basal planes carry no dangling bonds, so the iodine-terminated basal h-CuI plane cannot template γ-CuI. Moreover, the precursor species Cu and I are supplied on graphene and not on top of h-CuI, so a second layer cannot nucleate, which makes multilayer h-CuI (β-CuI) equally unlikely.

mechanism_principle.content: The discrepancy with literature corrugation values is attributed to simplification in the assumed vdW potential.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: which we ascribe to the unavoidable simplification in the vdW potential assumed in those calculations.

mechanism_principle.content: Equilibrium adlayers on open graphene explain the absence of h-CuI on open monolayers in wet-chemical synthesis.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Because such an adlayer is an equilibrium feature of the open graphene surface in liquid-phase synthesis, it offers an explanation for the absence of h-CuI on open monolayer regions in the wet-chemical route [26].

mechanism_principle.content: Residual oxo-groups, water, and iodine after 40 °C treatment limit crystallite size.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: After the 40 °C HI treatment the reduced oxo-graphene surface still carries residual oxo-groups, physisorbed water, and adsorbed iodine [35], limiting the size of the h-CuI crystallites.

mechanism_principle.content: The damping is attributed to strong spectral coherence between SLG and h-CuI out-of-plane center-of-mass motion.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: We attribute the damping to the strong spectral coherence γ2 between the out-of-plane center-of-mass motion of SLG and h-CuI

mechanism_principle.content: The vdW spring from graphene sets the frequency scale of the collective out-of-plane mode.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The same adhesion well depth used in the preceding section therefore also sets the expected frequency scale of this collective out-of-plane motion.

mechanism_principle.content: Large biaxial-to-uniaxial strain-cost anisotropy explains experimentally preferred uniaxial adaptation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This anisotropy factor [Eq. (S8)] helps explain the preference for uniaxial adaptation observed experimentally.

mechanism_principle.content: An adsorbed water layer is comparable in thickness to the equilibrium gap, so it can strongly weaken vdW adhesion.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: An interfacial layer, such as the adsorbed water layer, 3.7 ± 0.2 Å thick [S15], that is ubiquitous on graphitic surfaces under ambient conditions [S16], is comparable to z0 itself.

hypothesis_statement.content: The oxo-G template retains sufficient periodicity to support vdW epitaxy.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: These well-defined crystallographic signatures demonstrate that the oxo-G retains the lattice periodicity required to act as a robust template for van der Waals (vdW) epitaxy.

evidence_result.content: Control on a gold grid produced no h-CuI, supporting that copper comes only from the copper grid.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The copper originates solely from the grid: a control synthesis on a gold (Au) TEM grid, under otherwise identical conditions, yields no h-CuI

evidence_result.content: HRTEM and FFT show oxo-G retains long-range crystallinity and bilayer twist structure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The FFT analysis in Fig. 2(f) shows two discrete sets of sharp hexagonal reflections, labeled G and G′, corresponding to a relative twist angle of 16.7 ± 1.0°.

evidence_result.content: HI treatment alone yields discrete ~5 nm h-CuI crystallites on mono- and bilayer r-oxo-G.
evidence_result.evidence_span: HRTEM imaging revealed the nucleation of discrete h-CuI crystallites of about 5 nm on monolayer and bilayer r-oxo-G.

evidence_result.content: Post-annealing HRTEM/FFT show larger domains and sharper diffraction spots.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Post-annealing HRTEM imaging [Fig. 3(d)] reveals increased domain sizes and sharper diffraction spots [Fig. 3(e)]

evidence_result.content: h-CuI adapts uniaxially to graphene, with one direction commensurate and the perpendicular direction near intrinsic spacing.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The adaptation is uniaxial: along one direction an h-CuI vector matches the substrate period, while the perpendicular vector stays close to the intrinsic h-CuI value and retains a residual mismatch of about 1.4% (from the initial 1.67% lattice mismatch).

evidence_result.content: h-CuI also nucleates within bilayer graphene after HI treatment.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Following HI treatment at 40 °C, h-CuI nucleation is also observed within bilayer regions.

evidence_result.content: Growth on monolayer and bilayer proceeds analogously, both yielding epitaxial hexagonal h-CuI.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In both, h-CuI grows epitaxially with a hexagonal lattice, which shows that intercalation into twisted bilayer graphene proceeds analogously to growth on the open monolayer surface.

evidence_result.content: STEM-EDX/HAADF reveal extended h-CuI areas on graphene after annealing.
evidence_result.evidence_span: High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) imaging [Fig. 5(a)] — complemented by elemental mapping, see Supporting Information [Fig. S1] — reveals extended areas of h-CuI over several hundred nanometers on the graphene membrane.

evidence_result.content: Cu and I co-localize in crystal regions while carbon remains uniform.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The composite EDX elemental map [Fig. 5(c)] shows copper (Cu) and iodine (I) co-localized in the regions where crystals have formed, while the carbon (C) signal remains uniform across the graphene template.

evidence_result.content: EDX gives a Cu:I ratio consistent with CuI stoichiometry.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The resulting Cu:I ratio of 1.4 ± 0.3 is consistent with the 1:1 stoichiometry of copper(I) iodide within the accuracy of standardless EDX quantification.

evidence_result.content: Sulfur and sodium were not detected, suggesting efficient SDS removal and a clean template.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Sulfur (from the SDS surfactant) and sodium were not detected within the signal-to-noise limits of the current EDX acquisition. This suggests an efficient removal of SDS surfactant

evidence_result.content: Formation-energy estimates indicate h-CuI is metastable.
evidence_result.evidence_span: An estimate of the formation energies indicates that h-CuI is metastable.

evidence_result.content: DFT shows h-CuI monolayer on SLG is energetically less favorable than bulk γ-CuI, while encapsulation would favor it.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Thus, the h-CuI monolayer on SLG is energetically about 7.0 meV/Å2 less favorable than γ-CuI. A graphene-encapsulated h-CuI monolayer would be more favorable than γ-CuI by 6.6 meV/Å2.

evidence_result.content: Observed anisotropy implies h-CuI adapts only uniaxially.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The experimentally observed anisotropy of 1.4 – 1.7% over extended crystalline domains, see Table S1, shows that h-CuI adapts only uniaxially.

evidence_result.content: A tested defective graphene configuration changes adhesion by only 0.5%, leaving the energy balance effectively unchanged.
evidence_result.evidence_span: DFT calculations for a defective graphene substrate (Methods) give an adhesion of 13.65 meV/Å2, only 0.5% above the pristine value of 13.58 meV/Å2; the single defective configuration examined therefore leaves the balance of Eq. (1) unchanged.

evidence_result.content: At 180 °C coalesced domains and cleaner EDX signatures correlate with larger growth.
evidence_result.evidence_span: At 180 °C, coalesced domains form (Fig. 3; Fig. 5), and STEM-EDX records a cleaner interface, with the oxygen signal dropping and sulfur and sodium falling below the detection limit (Fig. S1).

evidence_result.content: Power spectra show much lower normalized out-of-plane antisymmetric motion on SLG than in BLG in the 1.20–1.55 THz band.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Between 1.20 and 1.55 THz the oscillation in BLG-encapsulated and SLG-supported h-CuI shows a mean normalized power of 0.288 ± 0.074 and 0.028 ± 0.022, respectively

evidence_result.content: Pair distribution functions show the hexagonal lattice is retained at 300 K on both SLG and BLG.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The characteristic maxima in the distribution functions show that the hexagonal lattice is retained at 300 K both on SLG and within BLG.

evidence_result.content: At 600 K iodine remains localized while Cu becomes more dynamic.
evidence_result.evidence_span: At 600 K the iodine atoms remain strongly localized, while the Cu atoms show increased dynamics.

evidence_result.content: AIMD trajectories show 2D h-CuI remains dynamically stable on open graphene and in bilayer graphene at 300 and 600 K.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The trajectories show that 2D h-CuI remains dynamically stable not only within a graphene sandwich but also on an open graphene surface at both 300 and 600 K.

evidence_result.content: Control synthesis on gold grids produced no h-CuI crystals.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Under these conditions, no h-CuI crystals were observed.

evidence_result.content: EDX shows reduced oxygen content in crystal regions after annealing.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Oxygen EDX map (O-K), showing reduced oxygen content in the crystal regions after annealing.

evidence_result.content: Two bilayer crystallites in the same flake align to different graphene sheets.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Sample 4 is nevertheless locked at the commensurate 30° orientation to G′ and Sample 5 to G, each keeping 21.7 ± 1.0° to the respective other sheet

evidence_result.content: FFT shows the additional bilayer h-CuI crystal aligns with graphene layer G, not G′.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The crystal therefore adopts epitaxial alignment with G rather than with the second graphene layer G′.

evidence_result.content: Measured anisotropy matches the laterally free uniaxial prediction, not the laterally constrained one.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The measured lattice anisotropy of the two annealed, graphene-aligned crystallites, 1.017 ± 0.004 (Sample 4) and 1.019 ± 0.004 (Sample 5, Table S1), matches the laterally free prediction of 1.018 rather than the laterally constrained value of 1.012

evidence_result.content: Observed contraction in Sample 5 supports perpendicular Poisson contraction.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The contraction seen in Sample 5 (b ≈ 4.18 Å < aCuI = 4.19 Å, Table S1) confirms the perpendicular Poisson contraction.

evidence_result.content: Calculated adhesion is nearly the same for pristine and defective graphene.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The calculated values are 13.58 meV/Å2 (0.218 J/m2) for pristine graphene and 13.65 meV/Å2 for defective graphene.

evidence_result.content: Adding a 2.8–3.7 Å gap lowers adhesion to 2.3 or 1.4 meV/Å2, i.e. 17% or 10% of the original.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Evaluating EvdW(z0 + Δz) for an additional gap Δz = 2.8–3.7 Å gives 2.3 meV/Å2 at Δz = 2.8 Å and 1.4 meV/Å2 at Δz = 3.7 Å, that is 17% and 10% of E0.

evidence_result.content: Supported h-CuI follows graphene out-of-plane motion more closely than encapsulated pairs do.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The supported h-CuI sheet follows the out-of-plane motion of its graphene layer more closely than either pair of the encapsulated cell.

constraint.content: Observed uniaxial strain constrains the epitaxial energy balance.
constraint.evidence_span: The observation of uniaxial strain in the extended h-CuI crystals (Samples 2, 4, and 5, and Ref. [26]) provides a constraint on the total energy balance for epitaxial growth of the 2D layer on graphene.

constraint.content: The corrugation gain must lie between the uniaxial and biaxial strain costs.
constraint.evidence_span: The corrugation gain must therefore exceed the uniaxial cost but stay below the biaxial one, 0.30 < ΔUP,eff < 1.05 meV/Å2.

constraint.content: The stiffer graphene substrate can suppress lateral relaxation of soft h-CuI in the laterally constrained estimate.
constraint.evidence_span: applicable when the stiffer graphene substrate (E2DGr ≈ 340 N/m) suppresses lateral relaxation of the soft h-CuI (E2D ≈ 35 N/m, Table S3)

constraint.content: The layer must accommodate the lattice mismatch as strain.
constraint.evidence_span: the layer must take it up as a strain ε = δ

constraint.content: A frequency can only be resolved if each segment contains at least one full period.
constraint.evidence_span: a frequency is resolved in a segment-averaged spectrum only if every contributing segment holds at least one full period of it.

constraint.content: The run resolution limit is 0.85 THz.
constraint.evidence_span: the resolution limit of a run is set by the largest of these, 0.85 THz.

constraint.content: Longer time scales are inaccessible because restart segments are only about 1.5 ps.
constraint.evidence_span: Time scales beyond the restart segments are outside the reach of these trajectories.

contradiction.content: The inferred lower bound on corrugation exceeds literature DFT values by about a factor of two.
contradiction.evidence_span: The lower bound inferred from the observed uniaxial strain exceeds the corrugation amplitudes reported from DFT calculations in the literature (≤ 0.14 meV/Å2, Table S3) [28] by about a factor of two

causal_claim.content: Thermal annealing reduces the oxygen signal, indicating removal of oxygen-containing functional groups and adsorbed water from the initial oxo-G template.
evidence_spans: Thermal annealing significantly reduces the oxygen signal in the EDX maps (see Fig. S1e), indicating the effective removal of oxygen-containing functional groups and adsorbed water from the initial oxo-G template during the HI treatment and subsequent annealing.

causal_claim.content: Small early-stage nuclei show little in-plane anisotropy because their small size and high edge-to-area ratio prevent the directional lattice adaptation seen in larger domains.
evidence_spans: We attribute the near-absence of in-plane anisotropy to the early stage of growth: the nucleus is small and has a high edge-to-area ratio, so its lattice has not yet developed the directional adaptation that characterizes larger, fully grown domains.

causal_claim.content: The observed anisotropy arises from uniaxial lattice adaptation to the epitaxial template, while h-CuI remains relaxed in the perpendicular direction.
evidence_spans: The anisotropy of 1.7% indicates the uniaxial strain profile, reflecting the lattice adaptation to the epitaxial template in only one direction, while h-CuI remains relaxed in the perpendicular direction

causal_claim.content: Differing registry of crystallites with different graphene sheets in the same bilayer implies the h-CuI is encapsulated in the bilayer gallery rather than on the outer surface, because an outer-surface crystallite could only register with the outermost sheet.
evidence_spans: A crystallite on an outer surface of bilayer graphene would be templated by the outermost sheet in both cases, so registry with different graphene layers would be impossible. Both crystals are shown together in one image in Fig. S2, identifying the h-CuI as encapsulated within two graphene sheets
Registry with different sheets from within one plane is available only in the gallery, which places the bilayer crystallites between the graphene layers.

causal_claim.content: The hexagonal h-CuI phase forms because the conditions required for nucleation of bulk γ-CuI do not arise.
evidence_spans: The conditions under which γ-CuI nucleates do not arise in the first place.

causal_claim.content: One graphene interface partially stabilizes h-CuI relative to bulk γ-CuI but leaves it metastable, whereas a second graphene interface lowers the energy further and makes h-CuI thermodynamically favored.
evidence_spans: One graphene interface (13.58 meV/Å2) reduces the energy difference of h-CuI and bulk γ-CuI, however leaving the h-CuI/SLG heterostructure still about +7.0 meV/Å2 above γ (metastable, kinetically trapped)
a second interface further reduces the energy difference to −6.6 meV/Å2 (thermodynamically favored)

causal_claim.content: Interfacial adlayers strongly hinder supported h-CuI epitaxial growth because increasing interface spacing causes adhesion to decay steeply, strongly reducing the van der Waals stabilization needed for growth.
evidence_spans: In contrast, interfacial adlayers have a pronounced effect on the epitaxial growth... An adlayer that increases the interfacial distance by Δz reduces the recovered adhesion to EvdW(z0 + Δz).
The adhesion decays steeply due to the z−4 tail.
Such an interfacial layer therefore strongly reduces the van der Waals stabilization required for growth of supported h-CuI.

causal_claim.content: A single interfacial adlayer reduces recovered adhesion to only 10–17% of the original, which is insufficient to compensate h-CuI metastability; where adsorbates remain, adhesion is not recovered and crystal growth stops.
evidence_spans: Inserting Δz = 2.8–3.7 Å into Eq. (2) leaves a recovered adhesion of only 1.4–2.3 meV/Å2, that is 10–17% of E0, which cannot compensate the 20.5 meV/Å2 by which the 2D phase lies above bulk γ-CuI.
where adsorbates remain on the surface, the adhesion term of Eq. (1) is not recovered and growth stops.

causal_claim.content: Within bilayers, van der Waals pressure expels some adsorbates into pockets and presses the layers together, supporting binding where adsorbates can be removed; consequently, domain size correlates with local interface cleanliness, crystals extend until the next adsorbate, contaminated regions terminate domains, and on clean interfaces growth is mainly limited by precursor supply.
evidence_spans: Within a bilayer, the van der Waals pressure expels part of the adsorbates into pockets [42,43] and presses the layers together, supporting the binding where adsorbates cannot be removed.
The lateral domain size therefore correlates with the local cleanliness of the interface, as seen in Fig. S2, where the h-CuI crystals extend up to the next adsorbate on the surface.
Where the interface is clean, further growth is expected to be limited mainly by precursor supply to the graphene–CuI interface.
The domains terminate where they meet these contaminated regions, consistent with the contamination-limited growth identified in the Formation Mechanism and Stability section of the main text.

causal_claim.content: Graphene mechanically constrains h-CuI dynamics: a single graphene layer damps relative out-of-plane h-CuI motion by about an order of magnitude and damps the nearby iodine sublayer; in bilayers both h-CuI sublayers are damped, while in single-layer graphene the damping is asymmetric and strongest at the graphene-contacting sublayer; a second graphene interface also stiffens the in-plane transverse optical mode.
evidence_spans: Thus, a single graphene layer damps the relative out-of-plane movement of h-CuI between 1.20 and 1.55 THz by an order of magnitude in normalized power.
The vdW spring of graphene thus damps the out-of-plane movement of the iodine sublayer in its vicinity.
In BLG this damping is observed for both sublayers of h-CuI; in SLG the damping is asymmetric and stronger on the sublayer in direct contact with graphene.
For this collective in-plane movement, a second interface stiffens the h-CuI sheet.

causal_claim.content: At 600 K, hexagonal order is maintained mainly by the iodine framework, allowing the copper sublattice to delocalize and exhibit enhanced in-plane mobility within that framework.
evidence_spans: The hexagonal order is still maintained at 600 K, mainly by the iodine framework, while the copper sublattice may delocalize inside it.
The copper therefore exhibits enhanced in-plane mobility within a framework maintained by the iodine sublattice.

causal_claim.content: SDS compression causes flakes to assemble into a stable, compact, uniform monolayer film.
evidence_spans: This process caused the flakes to form a stable, compact, and uniform monolayer film.

mechanism_principle.content: A thin adsorbed interfacial film/water layer is present because HI vapor originates from aqueous solution and oxo-group reduction releases water; since this layer is comparable in thickness to the equilibrium graphene–h-CuI gap, it can strongly weaken van der Waals adhesion.
evidence_spans: Since the vapor comes from an aqueous HI solution and the reduction of the oxo-groups releases water, a thin adsorbed film is present at the interface during this step
An interfacial layer, such as the adsorbed water layer, 3.7 ± 0.2 Å thick [S15], that is ubiquitous on graphitic surfaces under ambient conditions [S16], is comparable to z0 itself.

mechanism_principle.content: The preferred 30° offset arises from the energetically favored registry in which iodine atoms sit at the centers of graphene hexagons.
evidence_spans: Physically, the 30° offset reflects the energetically preferred registry in which the iodine atoms occupy the centers of the graphene hexagons [26]

mechanism_principle.content: Formation is controlled not just by thermodynamics but by kinetically/accessibly available formation routes.
evidence_spans: Its formation, however, is governed not only by thermodynamics but also by the available formation routes.

mechanism_principle.content: γ-CuI formation is suppressed because it would require nucleation of a 3D particle with dangling bonds and sufficiently high local supersaturation, conditions not provided in the dilute in situ process.
evidence_spans: First, the formation of γ-CuI would require a three-dimensional nucleus with dangling bonds... Thus, CuI forms in situ under dilute conditions, and the local supersaturation required to nucleate a three-dimensional γ-CuI particle is unlikely to be reached.

mechanism_principle.content: Multilayer growth is unlikely because h-CuI basal planes are self-saturating and lack dangling bonds, and because Cu/I precursors are supplied on graphene rather than on top of h-CuI, preventing nucleation of a second layer.
evidence_spans: Second, the h-CuI surface is self-saturating: its basal planes carry no dangling bonds, so the iodine-terminated basal h-CuI plane cannot template γ-CuI. Moreover, the precursor species Cu and I are supplied on graphene and not on top of h-CuI, so a second layer cannot nucleate, which makes multilayer h-CuI (β-CuI) equally unlikely.

mechanism_principle.content: The discrepancy with literature corrugation values is attributed to simplification of the assumed van der Waals potential in those calculations.
evidence_spans: which we ascribe to the unavoidable simplification in the vdW potential assumed in those calculations.

mechanism_principle.content: An equilibrium adlayer on open graphene surfaces explains the absence of h-CuI on open monolayer graphene regions in wet-chemical synthesis.
evidence_spans: Because such an adlayer is an equilibrium feature of the open graphene surface in liquid-phase synthesis, it offers an explanation for the absence of h-CuI on open monolayer regions in the wet-chemical route [26].

mechanism_principle.content: Residual oxo-groups, physisorbed water, and adsorbed iodine remaining after 40 °C HI treatment limit the size of h-CuI crystallites.
evidence_spans: After the 40 °C HI treatment the reduced oxo-graphene surface still carries residual oxo-groups, physisorbed water, and adsorbed iodine [35], limiting the size of the h-CuI crystallites.

mechanism_principle.content: The observed damping is attributed to strong spectral coherence between the out-of-plane center-of-mass motions of SLG and h-CuI.
evidence_spans: We attribute the damping to the strong spectral coherence γ2 between the out-of-plane center-of-mass motion of SLG and h-CuI

mechanism_principle.content: The van der Waals spring/adhesion from graphene sets the frequency scale of the collective out-of-plane mode.
evidence_spans: The same adhesion well depth used in the preceding section therefore also sets the expected frequency scale of this collective out-of-plane motion.

mechanism_principle.content: A large anisotropy in the cost of biaxial versus uniaxial strain explains the experimentally preferred uniaxial adaptation.
evidence_spans: This anisotropy factor [Eq. (S8)] helps explain the preference for uniaxial adaptation observed experimentally.

hypothesis_statement.content: The oxo-G template retains sufficient lattice periodicity to support van der Waals epitaxy.
evidence_spans: These well-defined crystallographic signatures demonstrate that the oxo-G retains the lattice periodicity required to act as a robust template for van der Waals (vdW) epitaxy.

evidence_result.content: Control syntheses on gold TEM grids produced no h-CuI crystals, supporting that the copper source is the copper grid rather than the substrate/solution conditions alone.
evidence_spans: The copper originates solely from the grid: a control synthesis on a gold (Au) TEM grid, under otherwise identical conditions, yields no h-CuI
Under these conditions, no h-CuI crystals were observed.

evidence_result.content: HRTEM and FFT show that oxo-G retains long-range crystallinity and its bilayer twist structure.
evidence_spans: The FFT analysis in Fig. 2(f) shows two discrete sets of sharp hexagonal reflections, labeled G and G′, corresponding to a relative twist angle of 16.7 ± 1.0°.

evidence_result.content: After HI treatment, discrete ~5 nm hexagonal CuI crystallites nucleate on monolayer and bilayer r-oxo-G, including within bilayer regions; growth in monolayer and bilayer proceeds analogously as epitaxial hexagonal h-CuI.
evidence_spans: HRTEM imaging revealed the nucleation of discrete h-CuI crystallites of about 5 nm on monolayer and bilayer r-oxo-G.
Following HI treatment at 40 °C, h-CuI nucleation is also observed within bilayer regions.
In both, h-CuI grows epitaxially with a hexagonal lattice, which shows that intercalation into twisted bilayer graphene proceeds analogously to growth on the open monolayer surface.

evidence_result.content: Post-annealing microscopy shows h-CuI growth/coarsening: larger or coalesced domains, sharper diffraction spots, and extended h-CuI areas over several hundred nanometers on graphene.
evidence_spans: Post-annealing HRTEM imaging [Fig. 3(d)] reveals increased domain sizes and sharper diffraction spots [Fig. 3(e)]

High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) imaging [Fig. 5(a)] — complemented by elemental mapping, see Supporting Information [Fig. S1] — reveals extended areas of h-CuI over several hundred nanometers on the graphene membrane.
At 180 °C, coalesced domains form (Fig. 3; Fig. 5), and STEM-EDX records a cleaner interface, with the oxygen signal dropping and sulfur and sodium falling below the detection limit (Fig. S1).

evidence_result.content: Elemental analysis supports formation of clean CuI crystals after annealing: Cu and I co-localize in crystal regions, the Cu:I ratio is consistent with CuI stoichiometry, oxygen is reduced in crystal regions, and sulfur/sodium are not detected, indicating efficient SDS removal and a cleaner interface/template.
evidence_spans: The composite EDX elemental map [Fig. 5(c)] shows copper (Cu) and iodine (I) co-localized in the regions where crystals have formed, while the carbon (C) signal remains uniform across the graphene template.
The resulting Cu:I ratio of 1.4 ± 0.3 is consistent with the 1:1 stoichiometry of copper(I) iodide within the accuracy of standardless EDX quantification.
Sulfur (from the SDS surfactant) and sodium were not detected within the signal-to-noise limits of the current EDX acquisition. This suggests an efficient removal of SDS surfactant
Oxygen EDX map (O-K), showing reduced oxygen content in the crystal regions after annealing.
At 180 °C, coalesced domains form (Fig. 3; Fig. 5), and STEM-EDX records a cleaner interface, with the oxygen signal dropping and sulfur and sodium falling below the detection limit (Fig. S1).

evidence_result.content: The observed lattice adaptation of h-CuI on graphene is uniaxial: one in-plane direction becomes commensurate with graphene while the perpendicular direction stays near the intrinsic h-CuI spacing, leaving a residual mismatch of about 1.4–1.7%; the measured anisotropy matches the laterally free uniaxial prediction rather than the laterally constrained case, and Sample 5 shows the expected perpendicular Poisson contraction.
evidence_spans: The adaptation is uniaxial: along one direction an h-CuI vector matches the substrate period, while the perpendicular vector stays close to the intrinsic h-CuI value and retains a residual mismatch of about 1.4% (from the initial 1.67% lattice mismatch).
The experimentally observed anisotropy of 1.4 – 1.7% over extended crystalline domains, see Table S1, shows that h-CuI adapts only uniaxially.

The measured lattice anisotropy of the two annealed, graphene-aligned crystallites, 1.017 ± 0.004 (Sample 4) and 1.019 ± 0.004 (Sample 5, Table S1), matches the laterally free prediction of 1.018 rather than the laterally constrained value of 1.012
The contraction seen in Sample 5 (b ≈ 4.18 Å < aCuI = 4.19 Å, Table S1) confirms the perpendicular Poisson contraction.

evidence_result.content: In twisted bilayer graphene, different h-CuI crystallites can align epitaxially to different graphene sheets; for example, one additional bilayer crystal aligns with layer G rather than G′, and two crystallites in the same flake were separately locked to G and G′.
evidence_spans: The crystal therefore adopts epitaxial alignment with G rather than with the second graphene layer G′.
Sample 4 is nevertheless locked at the commensurate 30° orientation to G′ and Sample 5 to G, each keeping 21.7 ± 1.0° to the respective other sheet

evidence_result.content: Energetic analysis indicates h-CuI is metastable: a monolayer on single-layer graphene is less favorable than bulk γ-CuI, whereas graphene encapsulation would make h-CuI more favorable than γ-CuI.
evidence_spans: An estimate of the formation energies indicates that h-CuI is metastable.
Thus, the h-CuI monolayer on SLG is energetically about 7.0 meV/Å2 less favorable than γ-CuI. A graphene-encapsulated h-CuI monolayer would be more favorable than γ-CuI by 6.6 meV/Å2.

evidence_result.content: DFT finds nearly identical adhesion for h-CuI on pristine and defective graphene, so the tested defect leaves the energy balance effectively unchanged.
evidence_spans: DFT calculations for a defective graphene substrate (Methods) give an adhesion of 13.65 meV/Å2, only 0.5% above the pristine value of 13.58 meV/Å2; the single defective configuration examined therefore leaves the balance of Eq. (1) unchanged.
The calculated values are 13.58 meV/Å2 (0.218 J/m2) for pristine graphene and 13.65 meV/Å2 for defective graphene.

evidence_result.content: Introducing an additional 2.8–3.7 Å separation strongly reduces adhesion, to 2.3 or 1.4 meV/Å2, corresponding to only 17% or 10% of the original value.
evidence_spans: Evaluating EvdW(z0 + Δz) for an additional gap Δz = 2.8–3.7 Å gives 2.3 meV/Å2 at Δz = 2.8 Å and 1.4 meV/Å2 at Δz = 3.7 Å, that is 17% and 10% of E0.

evidence_result.content: AIMD and structural metrics show that 2D h-CuI remains dynamically stable on both open single-layer graphene and within bilayer graphene: the hexagonal lattice is retained at 300 K on both supports, and even at 600 K iodine remains localized while Cu becomes more dynamic.
evidence_spans: The trajectories show that 2D h-CuI remains dynamically stable not only within a graphene sandwich but also on an open graphene surface at both 300 and 600 K.
The characteristic maxima in the distribution functions show that the hexagonal lattice is retained at 300 K both on SLG and within BLG.
At 600 K the iodine atoms remain strongly localized, while the Cu atoms show increased dynamics.

evidence_result.content: Out-of-plane dynamics differ between supported and encapsulated h-CuI: in the 1.20–1.55 THz band, antisymmetric motion is much lower on SLG than in BLG, and the supported h-CuI sheet follows the graphene layer's out-of-plane motion more closely than encapsulated pairs do.
evidence_spans: Between 1.20 and 1.55 THz the oscillation in BLG-encapsulated and SLG-supported h-CuI shows a mean normalized power of 0.288 ± 0.074 and 0.028 ± 0.022, respectively
The supported h-CuI sheet follows the out-of-plane motion of its graphene layer more closely than either pair of the encapsulated cell.

constraint.content: Observed uniaxial strain constrains the epitaxial energy balance for h-CuI growth on graphene; specifically, the corrugation gain must exceed the uniaxial strain cost but remain below the biaxial strain cost (0.30 < ΔUP,eff < 1.05 meV/Å2).
evidence_spans: The observation of uniaxial strain in the extended h-CuI crystals (Samples 2, 4, and 5, and Ref. [26]) provides a constraint on the total energy balance for epitaxial growth of the 2D layer on graphene.
The corrugation gain must therefore exceed the uniaxial cost but stay below the biaxial one, 0.30 < ΔUP,eff < 1.05 meV/Å2.

constraint.content: In the laterally constrained case, the stiffer graphene substrate can suppress lateral relaxation of the softer h-CuI, so the layer must accommodate the lattice mismatch as strain (ε = δ).
evidence_spans: applicable when the stiffer graphene substrate (E2DGr ≈ 340 N/m) suppresses lateral relaxation of the soft h-CuI (E2D ≈ 35 N/m, Table S3)
the layer must take it up as a strain ε = δ

constraint.content: Frequency resolution is limited by the restart-segment length: a frequency is resolved in the segment-averaged spectrum only if every contributing segment contains at least one full period; because restart segments are only about 1.5 ps, longer time scales are inaccessible and the run resolution limit is 0.85 THz.
evidence_spans: a frequency is resolved in a segment-averaged spectrum only if every contributing segment holds at least one full period of it.
Time scales beyond the restart segments are outside the reach of these trajectories.
the resolution limit of a run is set by the largest of these, 0.85 THz.

contradiction.content: The inferred lower bound on corrugation exceeds literature DFT values by about a factor of two.
evidence_spans: The lower bound inferred from the observed uniaxial strain exceeds the corrugation amplitudes reported from DFT calculations in the literature (≤ 0.14 meV/Å2, Table S3) [28] by about a factor of two
